title: Rolo and Jingle's Puzzle Door
markdown:
Rolo was a red panda, and his tail was the wiggliest tail you ever did see. It wiggled more than jelly on a trampoline. When he was happy it went wiggle-waggle-whoosh. Jingle was a puzzle elf, made of bright colourful pieces. When he laughed his tummy went rattle-tattle-jiggle-joggle. Sometimes his head went click-clack when he thought hard. He was the happiest, shiniest elf in the Whispering Woods.

One sunny giggly morning they were playing hide-and-seek near the Whispering Willow. “Rolo,” chirped Jingle, puzzle head tilting. “I heard a secret. A friendly ladybug told me there’s a castle made entirely of puzzles.”

Rolo’s tail did a happy dance. “A puzzle castle.” He did a little hop.

Off they skipped. Tap-tap-tap went Jingle’s puzzle feet. Thump-thump-thump went Rolo’s soft paws on moss. They followed a winding trail that glittered with dewdrop flowers. Jingle’s pieces chimed softly, like tiny bells.

They rounded a bend, and there it was: the most wonderful castle, big colourful pieces—blue sky, leafy green, bright yellow sun—sparkling in the sunshine. Dew still clung to the lowest pieces as if the castle had been waiting for someone slow.

The grand entrance was a giant puzzle door, and no matter how they tried, it would not budge. “Maybe it’s just stuck?” Rolo’s nose twitched.

Jingle, with a determined click, tried the big red piece beside it. “Not stuck. It’s a puzzle door, and it’s all jumbled. Pieces that should go together are far apart. Someone mixed up a giant puzzle.”

“Let’s fix it.” Rolo’s tail gave an extra-excited wiggle. “We’ll open it in a jiffy.” They grabbed pieces. “This red one with the pointy bit goes here.” A strange clunk. “This green leafy one looks like it should be near the window,” Jingle suggested, tummy rattling. They shoved and pushed, clatter-bang-whizz, fitting pieces super-duper fast.

The door stayed shut. It did not even wobble. The pieces were playing a stubborn game of not-fitting.

Rolo sat with a gentle plop. Tail drooped a tiny bit. “Oh dear. Still closed. I thought we were super puzzle solvers.”

Jingle’s bright pieces dimmed a little. He looked at the door, then at Rolo. “Maybe we’re doing it wrong.” He looked very closely. Jumbled, yes—but little pictures on some pieces: a tiny bird with a beak, a sparkly five-point star, a daisy with petals. “Rolo. What if we don’t have to be fast? What if we have to be patient?”

Rolo blinked his round panda eyes. “Patient?”

“Exactly.” Jingle’s tummy did a happy jiggle-joggle. Smile returning. “Let’s try again. Really, really slowly. Look at the tiny pictures. Find where they belong.”

They started again, a whole new feeling. No rushing. No pushing. Gentle searching. Rolo picked up a piece with a sunny yellow ray. “This looks like it belongs to that big yellow circle.” Jingle found a piece with a tiny blue wing and a little black eye. “This little bird needs to fly right here.”

They took their time. They looked closely at the edges of the pieces, and at the little pictures. They helped each other. Rolo would point with his nose. “Maybe this fluffy cloud piece goes here?” Jingle would carefully place it with his jiggly fingers. Click. Snap. Perfect. A ladybug—perhaps the same one with the secret—sat on a sun piece and did not hurry them. Piece by piece, they found where each belonged, and the door began to look like a picture instead of a jumble.

One piece left: a little sparkly star, shimmering. Rolo handed it to Jingle, tail a slow happy sway. Jingle found the empty spot and, with a tiny bit of sparkle, placed the star.

Click.

The giant puzzle door swung open with a soft happy creak, like a secret saying welcome. Inside: a big bright room that glowed warm. The softest fluffiest clouds, and the clouds were giggling. In the middle, a huge pile of delicious wobbly rainbow jelly.

They cheered. “We did it.”

The jelly wobbled as if it had been waiting for company. Rolo’s tail went wiggle-waggle-whoosh. Jingle’s tummy went rattle-tattle. A cloud giggled when they sat on it.

Rolo beamed. “You were right. Patient worked better than rushing.”

Jingle giggled, pieces rattling. They spent the rest of the day bouncing on giggling clouds and eating rainbow jelly, the happiest red panda and puzzle elf in the woods. The door stayed open, star in its proper sky, in case anyone else arrived in a hurry and needed the slow way.
